newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - March 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - March 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Industry analysts and major companies have denied criticisms by John Elliott that Australian companies are investing too much offshore and are neglecting onshore resource projects. Executive chairman of IBIS Business Information Phil Ruthven yesterday defended the decision of companies to invest overseas if that action maximised its profits. John Elliott made the comments at a speech he gave to a five hundred club luncheon in Sydney earlier this week. Page 5.

Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics yesterday show net foreign debt has risen by 3.2 percent to A$202 billion in the December quarter. Australia's overall liabilities to foreign investors now amount to over A$300 billion with net foreign debt now equal to 40.3 per cent of the nation's gross national product. This represents a 1 per cent increase in the figure recorded last year. Page 5.

Telstra is facing a challenge to its monopoly of the residential telephone market in Australia through the proposed alliance of eight large electricity companies which are negotiating to create a new national network with independent telecommunications company AAPT. The electricity companies will offer customers a single bill covering local, long-distance, mobile and on-line data services along with electricity costs all able to be covered using existing billing and service Centres. Page 1.

Crown Ltd shares fell a further 5 per cent yesterday amid mounting concerns over a massive cost blow-out in the Melbourne casino and angry reaction by institutional shareholders to a new A$180 million rights issue. The casino's costs are now expected to mount to A$2 billion Page 33.

Brierley Investments Ltd, the new major shareholder in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd has predicted the company will be a player not a target in any important shake-up of the Australian media industry. Brierley Investments Ltd chief executive Paul Collins said yesterday that Fairfax was a potential buyer of media assets and that Brierley would be happy to underwrite any reasonable acquisitions made by Fairfax, should restrictions imposed by cross-media ownership rules be relaxed. Page 33.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Crown Ltd announced its fourth major capital raising drive since early last year with a A$185 rights issue to charge up funds for a possible expansion of its A$1.55 billion permanent casino complex in Melbourne. Page 18.

Entertainment and leisure giant Village Roadshow Ltd is confident of maintaining continued profit growth after posting a 27 per cent rise in first-half net profit. The rise was credited to the success of the company's theme parks and resorts sector. The interim net profit of A$26.1 million was also supported by a 31 per cent rise in sales revenue to A$172.9 million. Page 21.

Insurance and banking group Colonial Ltd has restructured its accounts with a A$158 million write-off of expenses associated with demutualising and listing, ahead of its planned mid-year float. The write-offs cover all costs arising from the merging of the company's insurance and banking sectors and the statutory and professional advisory costs arising from the move to a public float. Page 20.

Brierley Investments Ltd has called for a review of company takeover rules following John Fairfax Holdings Ltd shareholders prevented it from lifting its holdings in the publishing group from 20 to 25 per cent. Brierley managing director Paul Collins specifically criticised legislation that required a company acquiring more than 19.9 per cent of another to launch a full takeover bid. Page 19

The share price of Amcor Ltd fell 14 cents, yesterday to A$8.35 after the company announced a 34 per cent fall in profit for the December half. Amcor, Australia's largest paper and packaging group blamed the fall on continuing low paper prices and demandfor other packaging products worldwide. Managing director Don Macfarlane said the industry conditions were unlikely to change until 1998 when paper prices were expected to recover. Page 19.

Gas and electricity utility AGL Ltd is expecting rapid growth interstate and in overseas gas markets after overcoming depressed industrial sales to announce a 19.6 per cent rise in net profit to A$75.6 million for the half year to December 31. The planned growth structure follows a major restructuring of the group which is confident of a continuing strong performance in the present half of the financial year. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Secret talks between rivals Telstra and Optus, are aimed at putting a halt to massive losses of up to A$1 billion in the pay TV industry, have hit the wall after Optus Vision told Telstra an agreement to stop building cable networks would be illegal and Optus would have little to gain from a cable-sharing arrangement. Page 25.

The Melbourne Casino Crown operator has announced a A$185 million rights issue, marking the third major capital raising in less than three months for the group. Institutional investors were irritated at the announcement as Crown shares dropped 12 cents to a 14-month low of A$2.16. Page 25.

Paper and packaging group Amcor has reported a 38.4 per cent slide in December half profit to A$131.5 million. Amcor has suffered intense competition in some operations and has responded with a plan which may see a merger of some of its product lines with outside partners to stimulate earnings growth. Page 25.

Australia's net foreign debt passed the A$200 billion mark in the December quarter for the first time. Australian Bureau of Statistics figures revealed the debt had increased 3.2 per cent or A$6.3 billion, to an aggregate of 40.3 per cent of the national ncome. Page 25.

The Australian Gas Light Company has posted a 19.6 per cent rise in December interim net profit to A$75.6 million. Sales for the gas carrier increased 8.5 per cent to A$492 million after an increase in its distribution network added over 14,000 to its cusomer base. Page 27.

Entertainment Group Village Roadshow has made a big picture of its 27 per cent increase in net profit to $26.1 million for the December quarter. The jump in net profit rode on the back of Australia's hunger for entertainment with a massive 31 per cent rise in sales to A$172.9 million. Page 29.
THE AGE

Country apparel manufacturer and retailer R.M. Williams has defied the downward trend in the retail sector and registered a 54 per cent jump in net profit for the six months to December. The increase represents net earnings of A$2.3 million and are up A1.5 million from previous figures. The company attributed the gains to strong domestic and international demand for its Australian products. Page B3.

The Brisbane-based Flight Centre yesterday announced a 34 per cent jump in interim net profits to A$7.07 million, from A$5.3 million previously. The discount flight specialist's chief executive Graham Turner said the company expected growth to continue in excess of 20 per cent after tax for the full year with shop growth of 15 -25 percent a year being forecast for the next five years. Page B3.

BRL Hardy Australia's second largest wine producer announced yesterday a 33 per cent rise in net profit to A$23.1 million for the year to December. The result has been credited to a record 1996 vintage, strong sales and a one off gain of A$2.8 million obained by selling its holdings in fellow wine producer Rothbury Wines. BRL Hardy shares rose one cent to A$3.16. Page B3.

The Amcor paper group has revived a long-term restructuring program to combat the continued flat outlook for world paper prices which suggest no increase in profits before the end of the year. Amcor yesterday posted a 34 per cent fall in interim net profts to A$140.6 million before abnormals. The result reflects a 14 per cent fall in paper prices in 1996 from the previous year. Page B1.

Institutional investors in the Crown casino company have protested strongly at the company's plan to make a A$185 million rights issue shortly after completing two limited placements at higher share prices. Crown said the rights issue would be valued at 1.80 a share, increasing the number of shares on issue by 103.9 million to approximately 727.3 million. Page B1.

Colonial Group announced its inaugural profit yesterday as a listed company, posting a proforma restated profit after tax of A$120 million for 1996. The figure does not include costs totalling A$158 million incurred in the restructuring of the group whic reduces the company's bottom line to a A$38 million loss. Page B1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
